summary:
**r8 source-only verdict: not accepted. Two blockers remain.**

1. **Cleanup can falsely verify release while an owned descendant survives.** [finite-cpu.ps1:46](Z:/Projects/OkuFlow/local-work-data/uct-review-implementation-20261023/merge/finite-cpu.ps1:46) starts its inventory with only the root child; descendant discovery begins during cleanup. If root → intermediate → compiler existed and the intermediate exited before that snapshot, the surviving compiler cannot be connected to the recorded root. Cleanup can then report `slotReleaseVerified=true`; the runner-lock probe does not detect a compiler that holds no lease. Preserve ownership across intermediate exits, preferably through a Windows job established before child execution.

2. **Cleanup does not enforce the absolute 900-second deadline.** [finite-cpu.ps1:6](Z:/Projects/OkuFlow/local-work-data/uct-review-implementation-20261023/merge/finite-cpu.ps1:6) performs descendant traversal and handle acquisition without deadline checks. [finite-cpu.ps1:67](Z:/Projects/OkuFlow/local-work-data/uct-review-implementation-20261023/merge/finite-cpu.ps1:67) also performs synchronous recursive `Kill(true)` without a timeout. The surrounding stopwatch checks cannot interrupt either operation. Make discovery and termination deadline-aware; the 30-second reserve alone does not bound them.

All current r8 pins, retained originals/r6 copies, 17 source hashes, three archive receipts and manifest/patch hashes match. Fresh AST parsing found zero syntax errors or reserved-variable writes/binders. Tracked arguments, expected FULL2 selection, cache rechecks and lease ordering passed static inspection.

No harness, probe, build or test ran; no files changed. Runtime behavior, compilation, equivalence and performance remain unverified. Compute remains **HELD**.
